correctness.rationale: A coherent rim cycle with n pendants has 2n arcs and a multipath face iff it selects at most one incoming and outgoing rim/pedant arc at each vertex and omits the complete rim cycle. Each pendant conflicts with exactly one rim edge; partitioning pendants by that rim arc yields local face factor (1+t)+(1+t)^k−1 for k=0,1,2. A cyclic orientation word with q transitions of each type gives exactly q k=0, q k=2 and n−2q k=1 factors, hence (1+t)^q(1+2t)^(n−2q)(1+3t+t²)^q−t^n. Uniform words give boundary crosspolytope (S0)^{*n} minus one facet, hence a PL (n−1)-ball. A mixed word has an in→out boundary giving rim arc e_j with no pendant conflict; pairing each pendant-bearing face not containing e_j with its e_j augmentation in descending lower-cardinality order is a finite sequence of actual free-face elementary collapses to all proper rim-edge subsets ∂Δ(E)≃S^(n−2). The rim inclusion intertwines any orientation-preserving cyclic rotation, giving sign (−1)^(n−gcd(n,k)) on top integral homology. Independently enumerated and compared complete direct-arc multipath face sets to local-factor predictions for all 8,16,32,64 orientation words at n=3,4,5,6, checked polynomial and each mixed relative collapse; the all-n proof is structural, not an extrapolation.
residual_risks: Coherently oriented rim, one pendant per rim vertex, n≥3 only; rotational statement not equivariant homotopy equivalence.

value.rationale: The directed sunlet is a canonical cycle-with-one-leaf-per-vertex family; its 2^n orientation choices pose a natural complete topological classification. The dichotomy is sharp: uniform pendants fill the rim sphere into a PL ball, while every mixed pattern simplicially collapses to the original rim sphere. The transition-count face polynomial and rotation character give additional concrete invariant structure. The proof supplies a reusable free-unconstrained-rim-edge collapse and is not an arbitrary small instance.
residual_risks: No classification of other core orientations, multiple pendants or bidirected rim arcs.
